title: Challenges to the social order

draft.title: Challenges to the social order
card: The social order is the accepted set of roles and ranks in a society, such as who holds power by class, race or gender. Between the wars, many people began to question it.
Class
Workers used strikes to demand better pay and conditions. In Britain in 1926, a general strike by many workers was called in support of coal miners.
Race
Groups pushed back against racial discrimination. In the United States, the Harlem Renaissance and groups such as the NAACP asserted Black pride and rights.
Gender
Some women challenged ideas that their place was in the home, by taking jobs, voting and joining protests. Challenges often met resistance and did not always succeed.
draft.remember: Between the wars, strikes, protests and movements questioned who held power by class, race and gender.

a.q: What was the main aim of workers who joined the 1926 general strike in Britain?
opts: To support miners facing lower pay and longer hours
To end racial discrimination in the workplace
To win the vote for women
To remove the king from power
a.why: The strike was called to support coal miners in a dispute over pay and conditions. It was a challenge based on class, not race or the vote.
a.clue: The strike was about workers and wages.

b.q: In 1925, Maya, a Black writer in New York, publishes poems that celebrate Black life and demand equal rights. Which challenge to the social order does this show?
opts: A challenge to racial roles through culture and protest
A challenge to class roles through a workers' strike
A challenge to gender roles through the right to vote
A challenge to government through an armed uprising
b.why: Maya's work asserts Black pride and rights, which questions racial hierarchy. It is not a strike, a vote campaign or an uprising, though she may also be a woman.
b.clue: Focus on what her poems demand.

a.best: To support miners facing lower pay and longer hours

b.best: A challenge to racial roles through culture and protest

problems.detail: The clue 'The strike was about workers and wages' practically names the answer. It is the only option about workers and pay, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

The distractors (votes for women, removing the king, racial discrimination) are implausible for a Year 11 student. The right option is also the only one with a precise detail ('lower pay and longer hours'), so the question is too easy.
Why (b) ends with 'though she may also be a woman', which is confusing because Maya is presented as a woman. It hints at a gender reading without explaining why that reading is not the best answer.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both intended answers are right. Question a is too easy, with a clue that gives the answer away and weak distractors, and why (b) has a confusing remark about Maya possibly being a woman.

proposal.title: Challenges to the social order
card: The social order is the accepted set of roles and ranks in a society, such as who holds power by class, race or gender. Between the wars, many people began to question it.
Class

Workers used strikes to demand better pay and conditions. In Britain in 1926, a general strike was called to back coal miners facing pay cuts and longer hours. It was not a bid for revolution, and it ended after nine days.
Race
Groups pushed back against racial discrimination. In the United States, the Harlem Renaissance and groups such as the NAACP asserted Black pride and rights.
Gender
Some women challenged ideas that their place was in the home, by taking jobs, voting and joining protests. Challenges often met resistance and did not always succeed.
proposal.remember: Between the wars, strikes, protests and movements questioned who held power by class, race and gender.

a.q: What was the main aim of the 1926 general strike in Britain?
opts: To back coal miners against cuts to pay and longer hours
To overthrow the government through an armed revolution
To win equal pay for women working in the coal mines
To demand a shorter working week for factory workers
a.why: The strike was called to support coal miners facing pay cuts and longer hours, a challenge based on class. Some feared it was a revolution, but it was not a bid to overthrow the government, and it ended after nine days.
a.clue: Think about which group the strike was called to help.

b.q: In 1925, Maya, a Black writer in New York, publishes poems that celebrate Black life and demand equal rights. Which challenge to the social order does this show?
opts: A challenge to racial roles through culture and protest
A challenge to class roles through a workers' strike
A challenge to gender roles through women's writing
A challenge to government through an armed uprising
b.why: Maya's poems assert Black pride and demand equal rights, which questions racial hierarchy, as the Harlem Renaissance did. Being a woman writer does not make it a gender challenge: her poems demand racial equality, not changes to women's roles.
b.clue: Focus on what her poems demand, not who wrote them.
